prompt: # Labeling instructions (given verbatim to each labeler) `sample.json` holds 100 edits that `specrot fix` proposes in 26 open-source projects. Each item has the original line (`old`), the rewritten line (`new`), what changed (`change`: old RFC and section → new RFC and section) and the code context (±3 lines). The replacements come from the RFC Editor's "obsoletes" data; sections are mapped by matching headings. Label each item independently, from its context only, with one `label`: - `correct`: a maintainer could merge this line as is: the text cites the old RFC as the specification the code follows, and the new RFC (and section, if any) says the same thing for this purpose. - `keep`: the old citation is deliberate (legacy behaviour, compatibility, history, a quotation, a list of supported RFCs, a protocol or file-format name); the line should not change. - `wrong`: the line should change, but this rewrite is wrong (wrong document, wrong section, broken text). When unsure between `correct` and another label, choose the other label. Add `note` (at most 12 words). Output: a JSON list of `{"i": , "label":
